cards.explanation: The answer is a help that is always there. The song says God is “…an ever-present help in times of trouble.” Ever-present means He's already in the room, friends. Nobody has to go find Him. That's like the friend who's standing in your kitchen before you even finish yelling about the smoke.

The answer is fear. Right there in verse 2: “Therefore we will not fear…” That word "therefore" ties it straight back to God being their refuge and strength. The earth can be transformed and the mountains can topple, and they still sing it. I'd be hiding under my apron at the first rumble, friends, so this is some serious steadiness.

The answer is delight. Verse 4 says there is “…a river whose streams delight the city of God…” After the waters that roar and foam in verse 3, the song turns to this river. The song also says it's the holy place where the Most High dwells. Streams that delight the city of God. I'd stand there with my hat off, and I never take my hat off.

The answer is False. Verse 2 allows for mountains toppling into the seas, but verse 5 says, “God is within her; she will not be moved.” The song puts those two lines side by side, friends. God is within her, and she will not be moved.

The answer is when morning dawns. Verse 5 says, “God will help her when morning dawns.” Morning is when the dark is done and the light comes in. I spent years in the dark at the back of a junk drawer, friends, and I can tell you the first light is a welcome sight. The song puts God's help right there at dawn.

The answer is True. Verse 6 says, “Nations rage, kingdoms crumble; the earth melts when He lifts His voice.” Look at who's doing the big thing there, friends. Nations rage and kingdoms crumble, but the earth melts when God lifts His voice.

The answer is that He is with us. Verse 7 says, “The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress.” With us. Right after the nations rage and the earth melts, that's the line the singers land on. Verse 1 called Him “…an ever-present help in times of trouble.”

The answer is the works of the LORD. Verse 8 says, “Come, see the works of the LORD…” It's an invitation to look at what the LORD has done, friends. It doesn't point at buildings or loot. It points at Him and His works.

The answer is False, and the song says so itself. Verse 8 calls Him the one “…who brings devastation upon the earth.” Then verse 9 says He breaks the bow and shatters the spear. Those are strong works, friends, not soft ones.

The answer is wars and earth. Verse 9 says, “He makes wars to cease throughout the earth…” Bows broken, spears shattered, shields burned. It all goes with wars coming to an end. A whole pile of broken weapons is a pretty clear sign that the fighting is done. That's not one town or one border, friends. The song says He does it throughout the whole earth.

The answer is that He is God. Verse 10 says, “Be still and know that I am God…” Here God Himself is speaking, and what He says to know is that He is God. After all that raging and melting in the song, that's the thing to hold onto. It's good news, friends.

The answer is the nations. In verse 10, God says, “I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted over the earth.” Nations were raging back in verse 6, and here God says He will be exalted among them. The nations and the whole earth are both named, friends.
